summary: Petition under Section 79(1)(c) read with Sections 142 and 146 of the Electricity Act, 2003 regarding non-compliance of the order dated 8.6.2013 in Petition No. 245/MP/2012 passed by the Commission and for consequential direction. The present Petition has been filed by the Petitioner, Dakshin Gujarat Vij Company Limited (‘DGVCL’) seeking the following relief(s): - _(d) initiate proceedings against Respondent No. 1 and its directors and officials under section 142 of the Electricity Act, 2003 for the failure on the part of Respondent No. 1 to comply with the order dated 08.06.2013 passed by the Hon’ble Commission;_ - _(e) direct the filing of the complaint in the appropriate court as per section 146 of the Electricity Act, 2003 for deliberate and wilful default and with the intent not to obey the order dated 08.06.2013;_ - _(g) Pass such further order(s) as deemed appropriate in the facts of the case._ _“49. In the light of the above discussion and after considering the views of Central Electricity Authority, the following directions are issued for compliance by all concerned:_ _(b) ESIL shall be granted status of a Regional Entity of Western Regional Grid._ _(e) ESIL shall comply with various provisions of Connectivity Regulations, Grid Code, UI Regulations and other relevant regulations of the Commission and maintain its drawal as per schedule._ _(f) All instructions of WRLDC shall be complied with by ESIL in accordance with the 2003 Act and Grid Code and any instance of non-compliance by ESIL would be viewed seriously and dealt with in accordance with law._ 6. Subsequently, AMNSIL filed two Petitions, i.e. Petition Nos. 1420 of 2014 and 1601 of 2016 before the Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission (‘GERC’) disputing the liability of Respondent No.1 to pay the Cross Subsidy Surcharge (‘CSS’). _Vide_ its separate orders dated 10.7.2023, GERC dismissed the Petitions filed by AMNSIL, and upheld the liability of AMNSIL to pay the CSS to DGVCL. 7. The Petitioner, DGVCL has filed the present Petition seeking directions in respect of the non-payment of CSS for the period post 16.12.2019 (i.e. vesting of undertaking of ESIL in Respondent No.1/ Arcelor Mittal Nippon Steel India Limited (‘AMNSIL’) pursuant to culmination of resolution process under IBC, 2016) which was a condition subject to which the Commission in the order dated 8.6.2013 in Petition No. 245/MP/2012 granted AMNSIL, the facility of direct connectivity to the network of CTUIL, the regional entity status, and the ability to have open access directly on interState transmission line for sourcing the electricity from the third party source. 8. The matter was heard at length on several occasions by the Commission, whereby both sides made detailed submissions in their favour. However, during the course of the hearing dated 7.5.2025, the Respondent AMNSIL apprised the Commission that the parties are attempting to resolve the issue of clearing the outstanding dues, and accordingly, requested listing the matter for hearing in the month of July, 2025. 9. The matter was again listed for the hearing on 3.7.2025, whereby the Petitioner and Respondent, AMNSIL, submitted that they have arrived at a mutual settlement and the issue of payment of outstanding dues has been resolved. On the request of the Petitioner, the Commission permitted the Petitioner to place on record the terms and conditions of such settlement as agreed upon between the parties. The Petitioner, _vide_ its compliance affidavit dated 9.7.2025, filed the joint application to place the terms of arrangement for payment by AMNSIL to the Petitioner along with the undertaking dated 9.7.2025 furnished by Respondent, AMNSIL. 10. During the proceedings on 29.7.2025, the learned counsels for the Petitioner and the Respondent, AMNSIL, mentioned that they have settled their disputes amicably and a joint affidavit has also been filed, in compliance with the directions of the Commission. Accordingly, the learned counsels prayed that the settlement arrived at between the parties may be taken on record and the Petition may be disposed of in terms of the same. 11. As stated, the Petitioner and the Respondent, AMNSIL, have filed a joint application dated 9.7.2025 stating that an amicable and unequivocal settlement has been reached between the parties, in terms of the undertaking dated 9.7.2025. Both parties in their joint application have prayed to take the said undertaking on record and to dispose of the Petition accordingly. 12. In view of the submissions of the parties, the joint application dated 9.7.2025, along with the undertaking dated 9.7.2025, is taken on record. Some of the relevant clauses in the said undertaking are extracted below: _4. Such payments shall be without prejudice to the rights and contentions of the parties in the pending legal proceedings of AMNS and DGVCL, disputing the applicability of CSS and in the interest thereon, before various fora (and any appellate or incidental proceedings arising therefrom). The list of pending proceedings are as under:_ _a. Review Petition Nos. 2243 and 2244 of 2023 filed by AMNS before the Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission;_ _b. Petition No. 186/MP/2021 filed by DGVCL before Central Electricity Regulatory Commission;_ _c. Appeal No. 13 of 2021 filed by AMNS before the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity;_ _d. Civil Appeal Nos. 2444-2445 of 2019 and 4488 of 2023 filed by AMNS before the Hon’ble Supreme Court._ _5. This undertaking shall be binding on the parties as well as their successors and assigns. AMNS is executing this undertaking voluntarily._ 13. In consideration of the submissions of the parties that all disputes between the Petitioner and the Respondent, AMNSIL, as raised in the instant matter have been amicably resolved in terms of the joint application dated 9.7.2025, along with the undertaking dated 9.7.2025, Petition No. 186/MP/2021, is disposed of in the terms of the above.
title: Petition under Section 79(1)(c) read with Sections 142 and 146 of the Electricity Act, 2003 regarding non-compliance of the order dated 8.6.2013 in Petition No. 245/MP/2012 passed by the Commission and for consequential direction. Dakshin Gujarat Vij Company Limited
